lens: Test-suite architecture — maintainability, duplication, runtime cost trajectory, fragility, hermeticity, -race coverage
rationale: The branch adds 321 test functions / ~16.1k test lines across 66 files. I judged it by execution, not by reading: I built three mutation probes against the spec's three mechanized anti-drift gates and all three went genuinely RED, including the agreement table under a mutation of the REAL derivation code (not just the doc). I found no test in the new surface that cannot fail. The five concurrency-heavy packages are clean under -race, and the new concurrency legs are not -short-skipped, so CI's `go test -short -race ./...` really does cover them. The largest new file (internal/complete/bead6_fixture_legs_test.go, 24 legs / 1640 lines) is properly factored onto two shared builders rather than copy-pasted, and internal/next's helpers are concentrated in one file. That is a healthy core. My findings are all maintainability-class and follow-up-shaped, with one exception I want recorded honestly rather than escalated: I initially measured the no-short cmd/mindspec suite hitting `panic: test timed out after 30m0s`, but on re-measurement that was self-inflicted load from my own concurrent probe runs, NOT a property of the branch. On an idle machine the same work runs roughly 3x faster and lands inside the budget. I am reporting that correction explicitly so no one downstream inherits my bad first number. Nothing here blocks the merge; every item below is a follow-up bead.
verification_performed: Mutation probe 1 (AC-5(vi)): added an unlocked `bead.MergeMetadata(id, map[string]interface{}{"mindspec_phase": "plan"})` writer to internal/complete in a scratch copy. TestMindspecPhaseWritesAllLockGuarded went RED naming the file, line and function. The gate is real.

Mutation probe 2 (AC-14): registered a new runnable cobra command on rootCmd in a scratch copy. TestVerbOutput_TotalCobraTreeClassification went RED with 'UNCLASSIFIED runnable command(s): [mindspec r8probe]'. The gate is real, and it forces cobra's lazy help/completion into the tree deterministically so its outcome does not depend on test order.
Mutation probe 3a (AC-2, doc side): flipped one documented cell in project-docs/user/guides/lifecycle-modes.md. TestAgreementTable_DocRowsCrossPinFixtures went RED with a doc-vs-fixture cell diff.

Mutation probe 3b (AC-2, NON-CIRCULARITY): changed the real derivation in internal/phase/derive.go (lifecycleInProgress > 0 returning ModePlan instead of ModeImplement). TestAgreementTable_Rows/next_(claim)_→_implement went RED reporting DerivePhaseFromChildren = "plan", want "implement". The table executes production code; it is not two copies of the same expectation agreeing with each other.

-race: `go test -race -short` on internal/phase, internal/complete, internal/next, internal/gitutil, internal/executor — all green (4s / 69s / 8s / 64s / 117s). No data races in the new lock, CAS, and snapshot-race machinery.

Hermeticity + can't-fail scan: scripted scan of all 66 changed test files for test functions with no t.Error/t.Fatal or with a single assertion site in a long body. All 27 hits were false positives from shared t.Helper assertion helpers (resultBeforeGuidance, probeEpicState, findUnguardedPhaseWrites) or from raw-string fixtures containing the token `func`; each was read and confirmed to assert. No test that cannot fail was found.

Every probe ran in a scratch copy under the session scratchpad, never in a checkout. The spec worktree is byte-identical at 8eaeb05e (git status shows only the panel review dir); the scratch copies are deleted.

findings.title: Ten parallel beads each hand-rolled the same test scaffolding; six new git runners, three copies of the draft fixture, and two repo-root walkers inside a single package
findings.detail: This is the class the per-bead panels structurally could not see, because each copy looked reasonable inside its own bead. Concretely: (a) SIX new, functionally identical git-runner helpers were added — internal/phase/agreement_table_test.go:224 `runGitCmd`, internal/resolve/draft_test.go:68 `runGitCmd` (same name, different package), internal/next/readyset_test.go:17 `runGitCmdForNext`, internal/gitutil/materialize_test.go:459 `mustRunGit`, internal/executor/materialize_seam_test.go:20 `runGitForMaterializeSeam`, internal/instruct/run_arrival_points_test.go:75 `runGit`. All do the same thing: pinned test identity, CombinedOutput, t.Fatalf. (b) `newDraftFixtureRoot` exists three times, byte-identical apart from which runner it calls: cmd/mindspec/state_show_honesty_test.go:34, internal/resolve/draft_test.go:85, and internal/next/readyset_test.go:56 as `newDraftFixtureRootForNext` — whose own doc comment states it is 'duplicated here since that helper is unexported in another package'. (c) `newBranchOnlyDraftFixture` is duplicated at cmd/mindspec/state_show_honesty_test.go:464 and internal/resolve/draft_test.go:367; I diffed them and the only differences are the runner name and comment prose. This one is not cheap — it does `git worktree add` + commit + `git worktree remove` per call. (d) Most tellingly, internal/phase now carries TWO repo-root walkers in the SAME package, added by two different beads: `repoRootForTest` (agreement_table_test.go:1076, bead 4) and `phasePkgTestRepoRoot` (sanctioned_sync_test.go:200, bead 2). There is no cross-package-import excuse for these, and they are not even equivalent — `repoRootForTest` stops at the FIRST go.mod walking up, while `phasePkgTestRepoRoot` requires the go.mod to declare the mindspec module. The former is the weaker implementation and would resolve wrongly under any nested module. Repo-wide the totals are now 18 repo-root walkers and 18 git-runner helpers. The plan never discussed test-helper sharing (no mention of testutil/consolidation/shared helpers anywhere in plan.md), so this is emergent, not a deliberate trade.
findings.recommendation: Follow-up bead: add an `internal/testutil` package exporting RepoRoot(t), RunGit(t, dir, ...), NewGitRepo(t), NewDraftFixture(t, specID), NewBranchOnlyDraftFixture(t, specID). That collapses the six new runners, the three draft builders, and the two same-package walkers, and gives the next spec one obvious place to add fixtures instead of a seventh copy. At minimum, delete one of the two internal/phase walkers now — that one is a pure in-package duplicate with a correctness delta.

findings.title: The bd epic-registry stub and the valid spec/plan fixtures were forked between cmd/mindspec and internal/harness with nothing enforcing they stay in sync
findings.detail: Unlike R8-1 this duplication is load-bearing for what the tests actually prove. cmd/mindspec/verb_output_test.go:486 `stubApproveBeadsForVerbTest` is an admitted reproduction of internal/harness/lifecycle_scenario_test.go:70 `stubApproveBeadsWithEpicRegistry` ('reproduced here since that helper is unexported in package harness and unreachable from cmd/mindspec'), and verb_output_test.go:454/469 `validVerbFixtureSpecMD`/`validVerbFixturePlanMD` reproduce harness's `validSpecMD`/`validPlanMD` at :289/:345. Two things make this more than cosmetic. First, bead 2's new `phase.SetMergeMetadataForTest` no-op had to be added to BOTH stub copies to keep them hermetic — it landed in both this time, but only because a human noticed. Second, the fixture markdown must keep satisfying validate.ValidateSpec/ValidatePlan; a schema change now has to be applied in at least two places or one suite starts testing against a spec shape the validator rejects. If the copies drift, AC-14's verb tests and the harness lifecycle scenarios silently disagree about what bd does, and both keep passing.
findings.recommendation: Export the epic-registry stub and the valid spec/plan fixture builders from a shared test-support package (the same one R8-1 proposes) so there is exactly one definition of 'what a healthy bd looks like to a test' and one definition of a schema-valid spec/plan fixture.

findings.title: The mid-run fix for the -short blind spot that 'bit TWICE' lives only in this run's orchestration prompts, so it evaporates when the spec closes
findings.detail: The BRIEF records that a no-short-only cmd/mindspec failure escaped two per-bead gates, and that the no-short cmd/mindspec suite (-timeout 30m) was therefore ADDED to the per-bead gate mid-run. I checked whether that remedy was written down anywhere durable, and it is not. Makefile:14 is `go test -short ./...`. .github/workflows/ci.yml:65 is `go test -short -race -coverprofile=... ./...` — CI never runs anything without -short. AGENTS.md:155 says only 'a bead's full `go test ./...`'. Every one of the ten per-bead Verification blocks in plan.md says `go test ./... -short`, and plan.md:1181 states the AC-13 method gate as 'final whole-tree `go test ./... -short`'. AC-13's own text is satisfied literally — the branch added zero new testing.Short() skips, so its new tests genuinely do run under -short — but the remedy for the blind spot itself is process-only. The blind spot it protects is real and measurable: 34 testing.Short() skip sites remain, concentrated in internal/harness (20+ TestLLM_* lifecycle scenarios) and cmd/mindspec (bead_clarify, otel subprocess, next_ready_gate legs), and none of them run in CI at all. The branch then added eight more heavyweight tests into that invisible tier: all 8 TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_* tests skip under -short via cmd/mindspec/next_ready_gate_test.go:57, so bead 7's headline #179 fix is pinned end-to-end only by tests CI never executes. The layering itself is defensible — internal/next/guard_test.go carries AC-8's unit legs and is NOT short-skipped, so it does run in CI — but the e2e tier only has value if something actually runs it, and after this spec closes nothing will.
findings.recommendation: Encode the gate rather than remembering it: add a `make test-full` target (or a nightly/pre-merge CI job) running the no-short cmd/mindspec suite plus internal/harness, and reference it from AGENTS.md's bead-completion rules. Otherwise the next spec rediscovers this the same way.

findings.title: The no-short cmd/mindspec suite is dominated ~75% by eight claim-guard tests, each building a full real-bd/real-git sandbox per leg at roughly a minute apiece
findings.detail: Measured, with an explicit correction to my own first number. FIRST MEASUREMENT (contended — I had a 10-package batch and -race runs going concurrently): the suite hit `panic: test timed out after 30m0s` having completed only 146 of cmd/mindspec's 335 top-level tests, with the 8 TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_* tests accounting for 1343s of 1795s elapsed (75%). RE-MEASUREMENT ON AN IDLE MACHINE: roughly 3x faster and inside budget — TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_UnrelatedDirtVariantsProceedWithNotice ran 167s clean versus 488s contended. So the timeout was my own load, NOT a defect in this branch, and I want that on the record so nobody downstream inherits my bad first number. What IS durable is the unit cost: TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_EnumerationPin measured in isolation on an idle machine takes 73.05s for ONE test, because cmd/mindspec/next_ready_gate_test.go:55 nextReadyGateSetupSandbox calls harness.NewSandbox (internal/harness/sandbox.go:41 — real `git init`, a full bootstrap.Run project scaffold, real bd) and then a real `mindspec plan approve`, once per leg with no sharing across legs. The claim-guard family builds roughly a dozen such sandboxes across cmd/mindspec/next_claim_guard_test.go, next_claim_guard_containment_test.go and next_gitignore_refusal_test.go. For contrast, `go test ./cmd/mindspec -short` is 30s. So runtime now scales linearly in claim-guard legs at ~55-73s each, and the next few legs added this way will push the suite toward the 30m ceiling on a normally-loaded developer machine even though it clears it on an idle one. Secondary, much smaller: cmd/mindspec/testhelpers_test.go:21 buildMindspecBinary shells `go build` into a fresh t.TempDir() on every call with no sync.Once caching — ~30 call sites at ~0.46s warm, so ~15s of pure waste. Worth fixing only because it is a two-line change.
findings.recommendation: Before adding more legs to this family, make the sandbox shareable — one bootstrapped sandbox per test function reused across its variants (or a package-level template directory copied per leg) rather than a fresh bootstrap + plan approve per leg. Cache buildMindspecBinary behind a sync.Once while you are there.

findings.title: captureStderr restores os.Stderr without defer, so a t.Fatal inside it strands the global for the rest of the binary — and I saw exactly that symptom once, unreproducibly
findings.detail: Reporting this at MINOR precisely because I could not reproduce it and will not overclaim. In one heavily-loaded run, internal/approve/TestApproveImplWarnStreamDefaultsToStderr and internal/complete/TestCompleteWarnStreamDefaultsToStderr both failed with 'warnWriter must default to os.Stderr, got *os.File'. Since `var warnWriter io.Writer = os.Stderr` is bound once at package init (internal/complete/complete.go:1586, internal/approve/impl.go:1154), that message means os.Stderr itself had been globally replaced and never restored by an earlier test in each binary. I could NOT reproduce it: green in isolation, green at the clean tip archive, green across three -shuffle seeds, and green at the merge-base. I verified my scratch copy was byte-identical to the tip, so it was not probe contamination. I am therefore NOT claiming a branch regression. What I can state as fact is the fragile shape that would produce exactly this symptom: internal/complete/complete_test.go:2063 captureStderr does `os.Stderr = w; fn(); os.Stderr = origStderr` with NO defer, so any t.Fatal inside fn (runtime.Goexit) skips the restore and leaves os.Stderr pointing at a closed pipe for every subsequent test in the binary. internal/approve/impl_test.go:1790-1801 has the same non-deferred shape. The correct form already exists in-tree and was added by this very branch — internal/phase/derive_recovery_test.go:38 uses `defer func() { os.Stderr = orig }()`. Related and also new on this branch: internal/hook/readstate_test.go:42 and internal/instruct/run_arrival_points_test.go:67 add more os.Chdir-based tests, extending a process-global-cwd pattern that already has two filed beads against it (mindspec-7y4d, z4ps) and that blocks ever adding t.Parallel to these packages.
findings.recommendation: Convert both captureStderr helpers to defer-based restore (a two-line change matching derive_recovery_test.go's shape), and add `-shuffle=on` to the CI test invocation so order-dependent global leaks fail loudly and reproducibly instead of surfacing as a once-in-a-while mystery.

findings.class: coverage gap at an inter-bead seam
findings.title: Bead 2's hermeticity stub removed the only end-to-end coverage of the new EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 write at the ApprovePlan seam
findings.detail: internal/harness/lifecycle_scenario_test.go:127 (added by bead 2) installs `phase.SetMergeMetadataForTest(func(string, map[string]interface{}) error { return nil })` inside stubApproveBeadsWithEpicRegistry, which every harness lifecycle scenario uses. The stub is justified — its comment correctly explains that without it each scenario would attempt a REAL bd write — but the consequence is that the repo's only end-to-end lifecycle scenarios now no-op the v2 marker write that bead 2 introduced at ApprovePlan's ahead-of-preflight position. That write is consequently pinned only at unit level (internal/phase/semantics_v2_test.go). Nothing is wrong today; the gap is that the integration tier can no longer catch a regression where the marker stops being written at that seam.
findings.recommendation: Either add one harness leg that swaps in a recording (not no-op) merge-metadata fake and asserts the v2 marker is stamped at the ApprovePlan seam, or record the deliberate limitation in the stub's comment so the next reader does not assume the scenarios cover it.

positive_observations: All three mechanized anti-drift gates are genuine, verified by executed mutation rather than by reading. AC-2's agreement table is confirmed NON-CIRCULAR: mutating the real derivation in internal/phase/derive.go turns it red, so it is comparing the doc against production behavior, not against a second copy of itself.

internal/phase/writer_inventory_test.go is the best-engineered piece of test infrastructure on the branch. It has its own unit tests with DECOY REDS for three distinct evasion shapes (map-index assignment, const-bound key, helper-built update map), correctly does NOT flag rvalue index reads, and its header comment states its residual honestly ('this walker does NOT trace arbitrary data flow... not an adversarial-evasion guarantee') instead of overclaiming.

internal/complete/bead6_fixture_legs_test.go — the largest new file at 1640 lines and 24 legs — is properly factored onto two shared builders (setupRealGitFaultFixture, wireBeadWorktree) with per-leg executor decorators, not copy-paste. internal/next's helpers are likewise concentrated in readyset_test.go. Where beads had room to factor within their own package, they did.

Assertion style is behavior-oriented, not brittle golden-string pinning: the new files use strings.Contains and offset-ordering comparisons (resultBeforeGuidance compares the index of the result summary against the index of each guidance marker) rather than whole-output equality, so message rewording does not cascade failures.

-race is clean across all five concurrency-heavy packages, and because the branch added zero new -short skips, the new lock/CAS/snapshot-race legs genuinely execute inside CI's existing `go test -short -race ./...`.
